subject: maths
question: Pipe P can fill (2)/(9) part of a tank in 28 hours, and pipe Q can fill (2)/(7) part of the same tank in 12 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 6 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 8 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
**Given:**

Pipe P fills (2)/(9) of the tank in 28 hours.

Pipe Q fills (2)/(7) of the tank in 12 hours.

P and Q work together for 6 hours, then are closed.

Pipe R alone empties the water filled by P and Q in 8 hours.

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Work / Time

Full time = Total work / Efficiency

**Calculation:**

⇒ Time taken by P to fill full tank = dfrac{28 times 9}{2} = 126 hours

⇒ Time taken by Q to fill full tank = dfrac{12 times 7}{2} = 42 hours

⇒ Efficiency of P = dfrac{1}{126}

⇒ Efficiency of Q = dfrac{1}{42}

⇒ Work done by P and Q in 6 hours = 6(dfrac{1}{126} + dfrac{1}{42})

⇒ dfrac{1}{42} = dfrac{3}{126}

⇒ Work in 6 hours = 6 times dfrac{4}{126} = dfrac{24}{126} = dfrac{4}{21}

⇒ Pipe R empties (4)/(21) in 8 hours

⇒ Efficiency of R = dfrac{(4)/(21)}{8} = dfrac{1}{42} (negative work)

⇒ R alone empties full tank in 42 hours

⇒ Combined efficiency of P, Q and R = dfrac{1}{126} + dfrac{1}{42} - dfrac{1}{42} = dfrac{1}{126}

⇒ Time taken when all three work together = dfrac{1}{(1)/(126)} = 126 hours

**∴ Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in 126 hours.**
